question.worked_solution:
Notice that the logarithms share the same base. 

First, we apply the power rule to the first term to make the coefficient in front of each logarithm the same:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}{log}_{2}⁡64-{log}_{2}⁡({x}^{2}) & =1 \\ {log}_{2}⁡(64)^{1/2}-{log}_{2}⁡({x}^{2}) & =1 \\ {log}_{2}⁡8-{log}_{2}⁡({x}^{2}) & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we combine the logarithms using the quotient rule. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{log}_{2}⁡(\frac{8}{{x}^{2}}) & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Writing this equation in its equivalent exponential form, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{8}{{x}^{2}} & ={2}^{1} \\ \frac{8}{{x}^{2}} & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve this rational equation for $x$ using the usual methods.

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{8}{{x}^{2}} & ={x}^{2}\cdot 2 \\ \cancel{{x}^{2}}\cdot \frac{8}{\cancel{{x}^{2}}} & =2{x}^{2} \\ 8 & =2{x}^{2} \\ \frac{8}{2} & ={x}^{2} \\ {x}^{2} & =4 \\ x & =\pm 2\end{aligned}
$$

Let's now check for extraneous solutions by substituting back into the original equation: 

- Substituting $x=2$ back into the original equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}{log}_{2}⁡64-{log}_{2}⁡({2}^{2}) & \overset{?}{=}1 \\ {log}_{2}⁡({64}^{1/2})-{log}_{2}⁡(4) & \overset{?}{=}1 \\ {log}_{2}⁡(8)-{log}_{2}⁡(4) & \overset{?}{=}1 \\ 3-2 & \overset{?}{=}1 \\ 1 & =1\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $x=2$ is a valid solution.

- Substituting $x=-2$ back into the original equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}{log}_{2}⁡64-{log}_{2}⁡((-2)^{2}) & \overset{?}{=}1 \\ {log}_{2}⁡({64}^{1/2})-{log}_{2}⁡(4) & \overset{?}{=}1 \\ {log}_{2}⁡(8)-{log}_{2}⁡(4) & \overset{?}{=}1 \\ 3-2 & \overset{?}{=}1 \\ 1 & =1\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $x=-2$ is a valid solution.

Therefore, the correct answer is "$x=\pm 2.$"
